name: Hasp
tagline: Biometric optical fingerprint smart deadbolt lock
summary: Secures doors, lockers, and tool chests using an R307 optical fingerprint scanner, actuating a high-torque SG90 servo deadbolt upon authorized match with audio feedback and dual status LEDs.

parts.name: Arduino Uno R3
parts.why: Coordinates biometric template authentication, servo timing, and feedback alerts

parts.name: R307 Optical Fingerprint Scanner Module
parts.why: High-accuracy optical sensor verifying enrolled finger prints in under 300ms

parts.name: TowerPro SG90 Micro Servo 9g
parts.why: Physically drives the mechanical sliding latch between locked and unlocked positions

parts.name: Active Piezo Buzzer 5V
parts.why: Emits confirmation chirps for success and error alarms for unrecognized fingerprints

parts.name: 5mm Green LED + Resistor
parts.why: Illuminates green during authorized unlock cycle

parts.name: 5mm Red LED + Resistor
parts.why: Illuminates red upon unauthorized access attempt or timeout

parts.name: 5V 2A Regulated Power Supply
parts.why: Provides stable power with ample current capacity for the optical sensor and servo load

product.pageHeadline: Hasp — Biometric optical fingerprint smart deadbolt lock
bullets: Sub-300ms optical biometric identification with onboard 1000-fingerprint memory
Metal-gear compatible SG90 servo deadbolt linkage provides positive physical locking
Dual-color LED beacons (Green/Red) and acoustic chirps provide intuitive user cues
SoftwareSerial architecture keeps Uno hardware UART open for diagnostics and logging
Heavy-duty reinforced 3D printable case with concealed mounting hardware

buildSteps: Step 1: Print the Hasp housing and deadbolt sliding rack in tough PETG or ABS filament.
Step 2: Screw the SG90 micro-servo into the inner retention bracket and attach the horn to the deadbolt rack.
Step 3: Press the R307 optical fingerprint scanner into the angled front lid aperture with silicone seal.
Step 4: Mount the Arduino Uno board inside the base and connect SoftwareSerial leads to pins D2 and D3.
Step 5: Install the green and red 5mm indicator LEDs into the top bezel holes with current-limiting resistors.
Step 6: Enroll administrator fingerprints using the Arduino enrollment sketch and test physical latch traversal.
Step 7: Fasten the tamper-resistant lid with four M3 screws and mount Hasp onto your cabinet or locker frame.

Generated sketch.ino with 5-second automatic re-lock timer and biometric verification loop.

avr8js verified servo angles: 90 deg upon match (ACCESS_GRANTED), 0 deg upon auto-lock.
Generated OpenSCAD heavy-duty enclosure with integrated mechanical sliding bolt track.
Mechanical clearance check passed: 2.0 mm clearance along full 22 mm servo deadbolt stroke.
